headline: Culture is the shared beliefs, practices, and values that make groups distinct—and connect individuals to something larger
universal_truth: You swim in culture like fish swim in water; it shapes you even when you don't notice
fun_facts: Some cultures have no word for 'blue'—and their speakers are slower to distinguish blue from green
Individualist and collectivist cultures literally perceive images differently in eye-tracking studies
Culture can change quickly—the internet has created global subcultures in just two decades
discussion_questions: What aspects of your culture do you only notice when traveling?
How has your culture shaped your values?
What cultural assumptions might you be making unconsciously?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Why do Japanese bow and Americans shake hands? Why do some cultures eat with hands and others with utensils? Culture is the invisible fabric of shared assumptions, practices, and values that make groups distinct—and that shape you more than you realize.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often think our way of doing things is 'normal' and other ways are strange. But we're all operating from cultural programming. How much does culture actually shape us?
cliff.prompt: How much does culture shape us?

options.text: Culture shapes perception, values, emotional expression, and reasoning—it's like an operating system running beneath conscious awareness
options.response: Yes. Culture isn't just customs—it affects how you see, what you value, how you think. You're running on cultural software you didn't install. Awareness is the first step to examining it.

options.text: Culture affects surface behaviors but not deep psychology
options.response: Research shows culture affects deep psychology too—perception, reasoning, emotion...

q1.title: Invisible Until Crossed
q1.script: You don't notice your culture until you encounter a different one. The fish doesn't see the water. Travel, immigration, or exposure to difference reveals assumptions you didn't know you had.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Invisible Until Crossed"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Deep Programming
q2.script: Culture affects more than customs—it shapes perception itself. Studies show people from different cultures literally see images differently, prioritize different information, and process emotions in distinct ways.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Multi-Cultural Fluency
q3.script: In a globalized world, cultural fluency is valuable. Understanding multiple cultures lets you communicate across boundaries, avoid misunderstandings, and see your own assumptions more clearly. Difference is a teacher.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You swim in culture like fish swim in water. It shapes you even when you don't notice. Awareness of your cultural programming is the first step to examining it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 208. Tomorrow, we'll explore why we keep doing things—tradition. Until then, identify one cultural assumption you've never questioned.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Cultural Assumption - What's Invisible?
growTrack.activity: Identify one thing you consider 'normal' that other cultures do differently—meal times, personal space, communication style. Question it: why do you do it this way? Is it better, or just familiar? This practice reveals invisible cultural programming.
